meta.spec_reference: PKWARE .ZIP File Format Specification, APPNOTE.TXT version 6.3.9 (2020) - principally section 4.3 (general format of a .ZIP file), 4.4 (explanation of fields), 4.5 (extensible data fields including Zip64 0x0001, NTFS 0x000a and Strong Encryption 0x0017) and 4.6 (third-party mappings including Info-ZIP Unicode Path 0x7075); the PKWARE Strong Encryption Specification for the Decryption Header; the WinZip AES Encryption Specification (AE-1/AE-2, extra field 0x9901); RFC 1951 for the DEFLATE stream that compression method 8 requires; CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (ITU-T V.42) for the entry checksums. The template itself cites https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zip_%28file_format%29 at line 29.

schema_extensions.name: dotted keys for fields inside anonymous nested structs
schema_extensions.why: The schema keys entries as STRUCT_TYPENAME.field_name, but the decryption header is an anonymous struct declared inline at lines 417-432 with only an instance name. There is no typename to use, and three of its field names - Format, AlgID and Flags - collide with identically named fields of EXTRAFIELD, while Reserved collides with EXTRAFIELD.Reserved, so a single-level key would be ambiguous. Every path component is a literal identifier from the .bt.

schema_extensions.name: fixed_result / fixed_result_hex
schema_extensions.where: the EXTRAFIELD.Size, ZIPFILERECORD.AuthenticationCode, ZIPDIRENTRY.deDiskNumberStart, ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.elr64DirectoryRecordSize, ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64DiskNumber, ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD.el64StartDiskNumber, ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber, ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory, ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDiskNumber and ZIPENDLOCATOR.elStartDiskNumber entries
schema_extensions.why: Each of these is genuinely a derived quantity - a byte count, a disk index or a volume count - that nonetheless has exactly one correct value in a single-volume archive of the shape this template can produce. fixed_result records the constant so the rewrite step can emit it directly, while algorithm/covers/includes_self still document what the field measures.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead sub-keys: values_hex, comparison, case_line
schema_extensions.why: The dispatch peeks one 32-bit word with ReadUInt at line 618 and then compares it in a seven-way if/else chain whose arms are at seven different lines. A single call_site_line cannot express that the peek site and the comparison site differ, so case_line records which arm each signature belongs to - which is exactly the per-call-site information a value-mining pass needs to know that all seven literals share one peek.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead function value "ReadUInt"
schema_extensions.why: The schema enumerates ReadUByte, ReadUShort, ReadByte and ReadBytes. This template's only lookahead is ReadUInt at line 618, and it is the single most important one in the file - every top-level structure is selected by it. Dropping the key would lose the format's entire dispatch.

schema_extensions.name: unused_in_parse_flow
schema_extensions.why: EXTRA64FIELD is typedef'd at lines 289-313 but never instantiated - its only use is commented out at lines 543-547. The flag tells the rewrite step that these entries describe declared-but-dead code, so it may wire the struct up or skip it, but must not assume it is currently reachable.

schema_extensions.name: template_deviations
schema_extensions.why: This template validates nothing but the top-level signature set, and it disagrees with APPNOTE in fourteen concrete places: a dead struct with a wrong-width size field, a Zip64 extra field read as a fixed two-field struct, two scalar reads of what 010 makes an array, an AES salt length that silently defaults to zero, four unguarded length subtractions, a Zip64 end record gated on thresholds that match no real offset, a misnamed disk-count field, VERECORD reused where the high byte should be zero, signed declarations throughout, three offsets that are never followed, and a data-descriptor search that relies on an optional signature. A generator that imitated the parser's laxity would emit archives this template accepts and no extractor does, so these must be visible as data rather than buried in prose.

schema_extensions.name: cross_reference emphasis in generation_range rationales
schema_extensions.why: These four fields are not merely bounded numbers - they are the archive's only pointers, and each must be back-patched from a measured layout rather than drawn. The schema has no key for 'this must be computed after the fact', so the requirement is stated inside the rationale where a generator author will read it alongside the bound.

meta.structure_note: A stream of self-identifying records each opening with a four-byte 'PK' signature and NO container header: first every local file header with its filename, extra field and compressed data, then the central directory that indexes them by absolute offset, then optionally the Zip64 end record and its locator, and finally the mandatory end-of-central-directory record that every extractor finds by scanning backwards from the end of the file.

VERECORD.Version.description: ZIP specification version encoded as ten times the version number, so 20 means 2.0; the template's read function divides it by 10 to display it.

generation_range.rationale: APPNOTE defines version codes from 1.0 up to 6.3, i.e. 10 through 63, and each one declares a minimum feature set a reader must support. 20 (Deflate, the baseline every tool implements) is the productive choice; 45 is required for Zip64 and 51 for AES. Values above 63 name no published version.

VERECORD.Version.notes: The typedef is at line 67 and its read function at lines 69-73 formats it as `%1.1f` of value/10. PKWARE APPNOTE 6.3.x section 4.4.3: 'version needed to extract' - 1.0 for default, 2.0 for Deflate and folders, 2.1 for Deflate64, 4.5 for Zip64, 5.0 for DES/3DES/RC2, 5.1 for AES, 6.3 for LZMA/PPMd/Blowfish. A reader is required to reject a file whose version-to-extract exceeds what it supports, so setting it too high is the fastest way to have a generated archive refused.

VERECORD.HostOS.description: Code for the filesystem the archive entry was created on; it determines how the external file attributes are interpreted.
VERECORD.HostOS.notes: The enum is declared at lines 44-65. This byte is the upper half of the 'version made by' word and is meaningful only there - in a 'version needed to extract' field APPNOTE says the high byte is unused and should be zero. OS_FAT (0) is preferred because it makes deExternalAttributes a plain DOS attribute word rather than a Unix mode shifted into the high 16 bits.

EXTRAFIELD.efHeaderID.description: Two-byte identifier naming which kind of extra-field record this is; it selects the record's entire layout.
EXTRAFIELD.efHeaderID.notes: APPNOTE section 4.5: the extra field is a sequence of records, each a 2-byte header ID and a 2-byte data size followed by that many bytes. A reader must skip an unrecognised record using its size, which is exactly what the default arm at line 277 does. The enum is declared at lines 152-197 and switched on at line 231; five IDs have decoded layouts (EH_Zip64, EH_InfoZIPUnicodePath, EH_NTFS, EH_StrongEncryption, EH_WzAES) and everything else falls to the opaque efData branch. EH_extTimestamp is preferred: its payload is free bytes with no internal structure a generator must satisfy, unlike EH_Zip64 whose two uint64 fields must agree with the record's 32-bit size fields.

EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize.description: Byte count of this extra-field record's payload, excluding the header ID and this size field; it is the only thing that lets a reader skip an unrecognised record.
EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize.algorithm: byte count of the record payload
EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize.covers: the record data bytes following this field; it excludes the 2-byte efHeaderID and this 2-byte size field itself

generation_range.rationale: Used directly as an array bound at lines 243, 269 and 279 with no check, and it drives the enclosing record's extra-field walk: ZIPFILERECORD decrements a local by efDataSize + 4 at line 410 and ZIPDIRENTRY at line 505, so an inflated value overshoots the declared extra-field length and the loop terminates early or runs on. For decoded record types the size is not free at all - see the dependencies - and the subtractions at lines 243 and 269 go negative when it is smaller than 5 or 8 respectively.

EXTRAFIELD.efDataSize.notes: APPNOTE section 4.5: the extra field is a sequence of records, each a 2-byte header ID and a 2-byte data size followed by that many bytes. EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize.algorithm: byte count of the uncompressed file data; it supersedes ZIPFILERECORD.frUncompressedSize or ZIPDIRENTRY.deUncompressedSize when those hold the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel
EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize.covers: nothing itself; it restates the uncompressed length of the entry's data in 64 bits

generation_range.rationale: A 64-bit size that a generator must keep consistent with the payload actually written. Zip64 exists precisely to describe files above 4 GB, so the spec bound is meaningless for generation; bounding it with the compressed payload keeps the archive self-consistent.

EXTRAFIELD.efOriginalSize.notes: Present only when efHeaderID is EH_Zip64 (case at line 233). TEMPLATE DEVIATION: this template reads exactly two uint64 fields unconditionally (the offset and disk-number fields are commented out at lines 236-237), so any Zip64 record whose real shape differs is mis-parsed.

EXTRAFIELD.efNameCRC32.description: CRC-32 of the enclosing header's original filename field, used to detect whether that name has been changed since the Unicode name was recorded.

EXTRAFIELD.VendorID.description: Two-character vendor identifier of a WinZip AES extra-field record; it is always the ASCII letters AE.

EXTRAFIELD.Strength.description: AES key strength of a WinZip AES record; it determines the salt length that precedes the encrypted data.

evidence.snippet: AESMODE Strength;       //1 bytes   Integer mode value indicating AES encryption strength

EXTRAFIELD.Strength.notes: The enum is declared at lines 214-218 and switched on at lines 440-451 to compute the local lenSalt. This field is therefore load-bearing for the parse: it decides how many salt bytes precede ZIPFILERECORD.frData, and a value outside 1-3 leaves lenSalt at its initial 0, silently shifting the whole encrypted payload.

EXTRAFIELD.deCompression.description: The real compression method used before AES encryption; in a WinZip AES entry the enclosing header's own method field says 99 instead.

EXTRAFIELD.deCompression.notes: The template's inline comment at line 275 reads `//2 bytes The actual compression method used to compress the file`. Note COMP_WzAES (0x63) is excluded from valid_values here: this field names the method used UNDER the AES layer, so it can never itself be the AES pseudo-method. COMP_STORED is preferred because it removes the need to produce a valid compressed stream on top of a valid encrypted one.

ZIPDATADESCR.ddSignature.description: The four-byte data descriptor signature; the top-level dispatch selects this struct only when the peeked word equals it.

lookahead.note: One arm of the seven-way if/else chain at lines 624-668. This is the single highest-value lookahead in the template: every top-level structure in the format is selected by it, and the else at line 664 aborts.

ZIPDATADESCR.ddSignature.notes: LittleEndian() is set at line 614, so a signature constant such as 0x04034b50 is the byte sequence 50 4B 03 04 on disk - 'PK' followed by two type bytes, which is why the template's own header records the file's ID bytes at line 13 as `50 4B //PK`. The top-level dispatch peeks this word with ReadUInt at line 618 and compares it against all seven SignatureTYPE constants at lines 624, 634, 639, 644, 649, 654 and 659; anything else raises a Warning and returns -1 at lines 666-667, so an unrecognised signature stops the parse dead. The data descriptor signature is the ONLY one APPNOTE marks optional: section 4.3.9.3 says it 'may' be present and that readers should be prepared for either form. template_deviations.action: Emit exactly 44 so every field is present and DataSect is empty.

template_deviations.subject: ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory is misnamed
template_deviations.issue: APPNOTE section 4.3.15 defines the third field of the Zip64 locator as 'total number of disks', not a directory entry count.
template_deviations.impact: A generator following the field name would write the number of files and produce an archive claiming to span that many volumes.

template_deviations.subject: VERECORD is reused for 'version needed to extract' fields
template_deviations.issue: APPNOTE section 4.4.3 says the upper byte of a 'version needed to extract' field is unused and should be zero, but the template types frVersion, deVersionToExtract and elr64VersionToExtract as VERECORD, whose upper byte is a HOSTOSTYPE code.
template_deviations.impact: The template displays a spurious host-OS name for a byte that should be zero; a generator following the type would write a nonzero OS code where the specification wants 0.
template_deviations.action: Emit 0 in the high byte of every 'version needed to extract' field.

template_deviations.subject: every 32-bit and 64-bit size and offset is declared signed
template_deviations.issue: elr64DirectoryRecordSize, el64EntriesOnDisk, el64EntriesInDirectory, el64DirectorySize, el64DirectoryOffset and ZIP64ENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset are declared `int64`, and COMPTYPE is declared `enum <short>` - all signed, where APPNOTE specifies unsigned values throughout.
template_deviations.impact: A size or offset above 2^63-1 reads negative, and a generator respecting the declared signed types would emit only half the legal range.
template_deviations.action: Treat every size, count and offset as unsigned.

template_deviations.subject: no signature is ever verified against a literal by an Assert
template_deviations.issue: The only validation in the whole template is the else at lines 664-668, which raises a Warning and returns -1 on an unrecognised top-level signature. Nothing checks a CRC, nothing checks that a directory entry's deHeaderOffset points at a real local header, nothing checks that local and central copies of a field agree, and nothing checks elDirectorySize or elEntriesInDirectory against the directory actually present.
template_deviations.impact: The set of files this template accepts is very much larger than the set of valid archives, so its behaviour is no guide to validity.
template_deviations.action: Take every 'spec'-sourced constraint in this file as binding despite the template's silence.

template_deviations.subject: deHeaderOffset, elDirectoryOffset and elDirectorySize are never followed
template_deviations.issue: The template parses the archive as a flat forward stream and never uses any of the three offsets that make a ZIP navigable - it never seeks to a local header from a directory entry, nor to the directory from the end record.
template_deviations.impact: All three can be arbitrarily wrong without this template noticing, while a real extractor uses exactly these values and nothing else to find the data.
template_deviations.action: Back-patch all three from the measured layout; they are the archive's only cross-references and the ones every extractor checks first.

template_deviations.subject: the data descriptor is found by a forward byte search
template_deviations.issue: When frCompressedSize is 0 and the descriptor flag is set, the template calls FindFirst for the S_ZIPDATADESCR signature at line 468 and takes everything up to it as the payload. APPNOTE marks the descriptor's signature OPTIONAL, so a conforming descriptor without it is invisible to this search.
template_deviations.impact: Any 50 4B 07 08 sequence inside the compressed data truncates the payload at the wrong place, and a signature-less descriptor is never found at all.
template_deviations.action: Always emit the descriptor signature, and avoid the descriptor form entirely where possible.

template_deviations.subject: COMPTYPE omits methods 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 20, 93-98 and 99 aliasing
template_deviations.issue: The enum at lines 88-110 lists 19 methods but skips several APPNOTE assigns (11, 13, 15-17 reserved; 20 deprecated Zstandard; 93 Zstandard; 94 MP3; 95 XZ; 96 JPEG variant; 97 WavPack; 98 PPMd version I).
template_deviations.impact: None for parsing - an unlisted value simply displays as a number - but a value-mining pass over this enum gets an incomplete set.
template_deviations.action: Prefer COMP_STORED (0); the enum's own values are all valid, it is merely not exhaustive.

template_deviations.subject: the FILEATTRIBUTE enum mixes two disjoint namespaces
template_deviations.issue: The enum at lines 315-357 puts DOS attribute bits (FA_READONLY through FA_VIRTUAL, in the low 16 bits) and Unix mode bits (kIFDIR through kIXOTH, explicitly shifted `<< 16`) into one flag set, and read_FILEATTRIBUTE at lines 359-379 ORs them all together for display.
template_deviations.impact: A generator treating it as one flag space would produce attribute words that are simultaneously a DOS read-only file and a Unix socket.
template_deviations.action: Choose the namespace from the host-OS byte of deVersionMadeBy and use only that half.
